Frances Ellen Watkins Harper, Iola Leroy.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/frances-ellen-watkins-harper/iola-leroy

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Frances Ellen Watkins Harper, the author, died 1911 (Wikidata Q5478699, P570 = 1911-02-20; the facts also list 1911-02-22, the same year).
- William Still, writer of the introduction, died 1902 (Wikidata Q3568976, P570 = 1902-07-14).

First publication of the text used: 1892 (SE colophon: 'Iola Leroy was published in 1892 by Frances Ellen Watkins Harper.'; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iola_Leroy says it was first published in 1892 in Philadelphia by the Garrigues Brothers and in Boston by James Harvey Earle, both in the United States).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1892, before 1931. A work published in 1892 entered the United States public domain on 1 January 1988. Standard Ebooks states the same in its rights statement below.
- Country of origin (United States): the text was first published there, so the US rule settles the origin whatever the death year.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
